headline: Margins and profit improve on lower sales; guidance raised
summary_short: BorgWarner's Q3 2026 sales fell 2.9% y/y to $3,487 million, but adjusted EPS rose 12.1% to $1.39 and the company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.20-$5.35.
summary_long: Net sales of $3,487 million fell 2.9% y/y (organic -3.1%) on lower industry production and weaker Battery Energy Systems sales. GAAP operating margin rose 180 basis points to 8.7%; adjusted operating margin rose 20 basis points to 10.9%. Diluted EPS was $1.08 against $0.73. Free cash flow was $195 million. The company cut gross debt by $864 million, bought back about $175 million of shares and paid a $35 million dividend. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance rose to $5.20-$5.35 from $5.05-$5.30 on buybacks and a lower tax rate; sales guidance was narrowed to $14.0-$14.2 billion.
confidence_notes: The shard's event sourceLink pointed at an unrelated 6-K, so the primary was found via search. The shard's EPS KPI is the adjusted figure ($1.39), so the diluted GAAP EPS comes from the release. Q/q deltas are only given for adjusted EPS (from shard). Guidance entries were not written to the event shard (no sanctioned script).

drivers.explanation: Sales fell mainly on declining market production volumes and lower Battery Energy Systems segment sales.
Continued cost controls delivered a higher margin despite lower industry production; prior-year quarter also carried larger other operating expense.
The increase was primarily due to a lower full-year effective tax rate and a lower share count after repurchases.
Guidance for adjusted EPS was raised on buybacks and a lower tax rate; sales guidance was narrowed because of lower industry production expectations.
